what_it_does: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) are a family of AI techniques that learn a 3D scene from photographs and can render it from any new viewpoint — useful for AR/VR, robotics, and photography. Running NeRF on a phone or headset (on-device) is hard because graphics processors (GPUs) consume too much power and area for that use case, and purpose-built NeRF chips designed so far only handle one specific NeRF variant well. FlexNeRFer is a custom chip design that handles several different NeRF algorithms by using a reconfigurable on-chip communication network (think of it as a flexible switchboard between computing units) and math units that can operate at different levels of numerical precision. It also skips unnecessary zero-value computations (sparsity exploitation — only doing math on the numbers that actually matter) and picks the most efficient data layout at runtime depending on how sparse the current workload is. The design was laid out in 28-nanometer silicon to validate its feasibility.
